title: Travel Landmarks
blurb: Places people travel a long way to see.

items.title: The Colosseum
items.fact: The Colosseum is an elliptical amphitheatre in the centre of the city of Rome, Italy, just east of the Roman Forum.

items.title: The Eiffel Tower
items.fact: The Eiffel Tower is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889.

items.title: Big Ben
items.fact: Big Ben is the nickname for the Great Bell of the Great Clock of Westminster, and, by extension, for the clock tower that stands at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London, England.

items.title: The Golden Gate Bridge
items.fact: The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate, the one-mile-wide strait connecting San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean in California, United States.

items.title: The Statue of Liberty
items.fact: The Statue of Liberty is a colossal neoclassical sculpture of a robed and crowned woman on Liberty Island, part of New York City, in New York Harbor.

items.title: The Taj Mahal
items.fact: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.

items.title: The Sydney Opera House
items.credit: Bernard Spragg. NZ  from Christchurch, New Zealand
items.fact: The Sydney Opera House is a multi-venue performing arts centre in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia.

items.title: The Great Wall
items.fact: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications in China.

items.title: Christ the Redeemer
items.fact: Christ the Redeemer is an Art Deco statue of Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, created by French-Polish sculptor Paul Landowski and built by Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa.

items.title: Machu Picchu
items.fact: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel located in the Eastern Cordillera of southern Peru on a mountain ridge at 2,430 meters.

items.title: The Pyramids of Giza
items.fact: The Giza pyramid complex in Egypt is home to the Great Pyramid, the pyramid of Khafre, and the pyramid of Menkaure, along with their associated pyramid complexes and the Great Sphinx.

items.title: The Parthenon
items.fact: The Parthenon is a former temple on the Athenian Acropolis, Greece, that was dedicated to the goddess Athena.

items.title: The Sagrada Família
items.fact: Basílica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família, or simply Sagrada Família, is a Catholic church under construction in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

items.title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa
items.fact: The Leaning Tower of Pisa, or simply the Tower of Pisa, is the campanile, or freestanding bell tower, of Pisa Cathedral.

items.title: The Brandenburg Gate
items.fact: The Brandenburg Gate is an 18th-century neoclassical monument in Berlin, Germany.

items.title: Saint Basil's Cathedral
items.fact: The Cathedral of Vasily the Blessed, commonly known as Saint Basil's Cathedral, is a Russian Orthodox church on Red Square in the historic centre of Moscow.

items.title: Mount Fuji
items.fact: Mount Fuji is an active stratovolcano located on the Japanese island of Honshu, with a summit elevation of 3,776.24 m.

items.title: The Grand Canyon
items.fact: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States. The Grand Canyon is 277 miles long, up to 18 miles wide and attains a depth of over a mile.

items.title: Niagara Falls
items.fact: Niagara Falls is a group of three waterfalls at the southern end of Niagara Gorge, spanning the border between the Canadian province of Ontario and the U.S. state of New York.

items.title: Stonehenge
items.fact: Stonehenge is a prehistoric megalithic structure on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, two miles west of Amesbury.

items.title: Neuschwanstein Castle
items.fact: Neuschwanstein Castle is a 19th-century historicist palace on a rugged hill of the foothills of the Alps in the very south of Germany, near the border with Austria.

items.title: Angkor Wat
items.fact: Angkor Wat is a Vaishnava Hindu and Theravada Buddhist temple complex in Siem Reap, Cambodia, and the largest religious complex in the world.

items.title: Petra
items.fact: Petra, originally known to its inhabitants as Raqmu, is an ancient city and archaeological site in southern Jordan.

items.title: Chichén Itzá
items.fact: Chichen Itza was a large pre-Columbian city built by the Maya people of the Terminal Classic period. The archeological site is located in Tinúm Municipality, Yucatán, Mexico.

items.title: Table Mountain
items.credit: Danie van der Merwe  from Cape Town, South Africa
items.fact: Table Mountain is a flat-topped mountain forming a prominent landmark overlooking the city of Cape Town in South Africa.

items.title: Tower Bridge
items.fact: Tower Bridge is a Grade I listed combined bascule, suspension, and, until 1960, cantilever bridge in London, built between 1886 and 1894.

items.title: The Space Needle
items.fact: The Space Needle is an observation tower in Seattle, Washington, United States. Considered to be an icon of the city, it has been designated a Seattle landmark.

items.title: Uluru
items.fact: Uluru, also known as Ayers Rock and officially gazetted as Uluru / Ayers Rock, is a large sandstone monolith.

items.title: Mount Rushmore
items.fact: The Mount Rushmore National Memorial is a national memorial featuring a colossal sculpture carved into the granite face of Mount Rushmore in the Black Hills, about 2 mi southwest of Keystone.

items.title: The White House
items.fact: The White House is the official residence and workplace of the president of the United States.

items.title: Times Square
items.fact: Times Square is one of the world's busiest pedestrian intersections, tourist destinations, and entertainment hubs.

items.title: Alcatraz
items.fact: Alcatraz Island is a small island about 1.25 miles offshore from San Francisco in San Francisco Bay, California, near the Golden Gate strait.

items.title: Old Faithful
items.fact: Old Faithful is a cone geyser in Yellowstone National Park in Wyoming, United States.

items.title: Half Dome
items.fact: Half Dome is a quartz monzonite batholith at the eastern end of Yosemite Valley in Yosemite National Park, California.

items.title: Lake Louise
items.fact: Lake Louise is a glacial lake within Banff National Park in Alberta, Canada.

items.title: Iguazu Falls
items.fact: Iguazú Falls or Iguaçu Falls are waterfalls of the Iguazu River on the border of the Argentine province of Misiones and the Brazilian state of Paraná.

items.title: The Moai of Easter Island
items.fact: Moai or moꞌai are monolithic human figures carved from stone by the Rapa Nui people, on Rapa Nui in eastern Polynesia between the years 1250 and 1500.

items.title: The Arc de Triomphe
items.fact: The Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile, often simply called the Arc de Triomphe, is one of the most famous monuments in Paris, France.

items.title: Mont Saint-Michel
items.fact: Mont-Saint-Michel is a tidal island and mainland commune in Normandy, France.

items.title: The Trevi Fountain
items.fact: The Trevi Fountain is an 18th-century fountain in the Trevi district in Rome, Italy, designed by Italian architect Nicola Salvi and completed by Giuseppe Pannini in 1762.

items.title: Saint Peter's Basilica
items.fact: Saint Peter's Basilica is a Renaissance church in Vatican City, and the largest church in the world.

items.title: The Grand Canal
items.fact: The Grand Canal is the largest channel in Venice, Italy, forming one of the major water-traffic corridors in the city.

items.title: The Matterhorn
items.credit:
Photo: chil, on Camptocamp.org 
 Derivative work: Zacharie Grossen
items.fact: The Matterhorn is a mountain of the Alps, straddling the main watershed and border between Switzerland and Italy.

items.title: The Alhambra
items.fact: The Alhambra is a palace and fortress complex located in Granada, Spain.

items.title: The Acropolis
items.fact: The Acropolis of Athens is an ancient citadel located on a rocky outcrop above the city of Athens, Greece.

items.title: Hagia Sophia
items.fact: Hagia Sophia, officially the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque, is a mosque and a major cultural and historical site in Istanbul, Turkey. It was formerly a church and a museum.

items.title: The Tower of London
items.fact: The Tower of London, officially His Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress of the Tower of London, is a historic citadel and castle on the north bank of the River Thames in London, England.

items.title: Edinburgh Castle
items.fact: Edinburgh Castle is a historic castle in Edinburgh, Scotland. It stands on Castle Rock, which has been occupied by humans since at least the Iron Age.

items.title: The Giant's Causeway
items.fact: The Giant's Causeway is an area of approximately 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, the result of an ancient volcanic fissure eruption.

items.title: The Cliffs of Moher
items.fact: The Cliffs of Moher are sea cliffs located at the southwestern edge of the Burren region in County Clare, Ireland. They run for about 14 kilometres.

items.title: The Forbidden City
items.fact: The Forbidden City is the imperial palace complex in the center of the Imperial City in Beijing, China.

items.title: The Golden Pavilion
items.fact: Kinkaku-ji, officially named Rokuon-ji, is a Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan and a tourist attraction.

items.title: The Potala Palace
items.fact: Potala Palace is a museum complex in Lhasa, the capital of the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

items.title: The Golden Temple
items.fact: The Golden Temple is a gurdwara located in Amritsar, Punjab, India. It is the pre-eminent spiritual site of Sikhism and its holiest site.

items.title: Mount Kilimanjaro
items.fact: Mount Kilimanjaro is a large dormant volcano in Tanzania.

items.title: Victoria Falls
items.fact: Victoria Falls is a waterfall on the Zambezi River, located on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe. It is one of the world's largest waterfalls, with a width of 1,708 m.

items.title: The Sydney Harbour Bridge
items.fact: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is a steel through arch bridge in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, spanning Sydney Harbour from the central business district to the North Shore.

items.title: Milford Sound
items.credit: Maros M r a z ( Maros )
items.fact: Milford Sound is a fiord in the south west of New Zealand's South Island within Fiordland National Park, Piopiotahi Marine Reserve, and the Te Wahipounamu World Heritage site.

items.title: The Empire State Building
items.fact: The Empire State Building is a 102-story, supertall skyscraper in the Midtown South neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States.

items.title: The Gateway Arch
items.credit:
St_Louis_night_expblend.jpg :  Daniel Schwen  
 derivative work:   ←   fetch    comms
items.fact: The Gateway Arch is a 630-foot-tall monument in St. Louis, Missouri, United States.

items.title: Mesa Verde
items.fact: Mesa Verde National Park is a national park of the United States and UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Montezuma County, Colorado, and the only World Heritage Site in Colorado.

items.title: Monument Valley
items.fact: Monument Valley is a region of the Colorado Plateau characterized by a cluster of sandstone buttes, with the largest reaching 1,000 ft above the valley floor.

items.title: Yosemite Valley
items.fact: Yosemite Valley is a glacial valley in Yosemite National Park in the western Sierra Nevada mountains of Central California, United States.

items.title: Crater Lake
items.fact: Crater Lake is a volcanic crater lake in south-central Oregon in the Western United States.

items.title: The Hoover Dam
items.fact: The Hoover Dam is a concrete arch-gravity dam in the Black Canyon of the Colorado River, on the boundary between the U.S. states of Nevada and Arizona.

items.title: Chateau Frontenac
items.fact: The Fairmont Le Château Frontenac, commonly referred to as the Château Frontenac, is a historic hotel in Quebec City, Quebec, Canada.

items.title: Buckingham Palace
items.fact: Buckingham Palace is the official residence and administrative headquarters of the monarch of the United Kingdom in London, England.

items.title: St Paul's Cathedral
items.fact: St Paul's Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of St Paul in London, is an Anglican cathedral in London, England, the seat of the Bishop of London.

items.title: The London Eye
items.fact: The London Eye, originally the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames in London.

items.title: Windsor Castle
items.fact: Windsor Castle is a royal residence at Windsor in the English county of Berkshire, about 25 miles west of central London.

items.title: York Minster
items.fact: York Minster, formally the Cathedral and Metropolitical Church of St Peter in York, is an Anglican cathedral in the city of York, North Yorkshire, England.

items.title: Durham Cathedral
items.fact: Durham Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of Christ, Blessed Mary the Virgin and St Cuthbert of Durham, is a Church of England cathedral in the city of Durham, England.

items.title: Bath's Roman Baths
items.fact: The Roman Baths are well-preserved thermae in the city of Bath, Somerset, England. A temple was constructed on the site between 60 and 70 AD in the first few decades of Roman Britain.

items.title: The Royal Crescent
items.fact: The Royal Crescent is a row of 30 terraced houses laid out in a sweeping crescent in the city of Bath, England.
items.place: Bath and North East Somerset, United Kingdom

items.title: Blenheim Palace
items.fact: Blenheim Palace is a country house in Woodstock, Oxfordshire, England. It is the seat of the Dukes of Marlborough, and the birthplace of Sir Winston Churchill.

items.title: The Forth Bridge
items.fact: The Forth Bridge is a cantilever railway bridge across the Firth of Forth in the east of Scotland, 9 miles west of central Edinburgh.

items.title: Eilean Donan Castle
items.fact: Eilean Donan is a small tidal island situated at the confluence of three sea lochs in the western Highlands of Scotland, about one kilometre from the village of Dornie.

items.title: Glenfinnan Viaduct
items.fact: The Glenfinnan Viaduct is a railway viaduct on the West Highland Line at Glenfinnan, in the Lochaber district of north-western Scotland, built from 1897 to 1901.

items.title: Loch Ness
items.fact: Loch Ness is a large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands. It takes its name from the River Ness, which flows from the northern end.

items.title: Ben Nevis
items.fact: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in Scotland, the United Kingdom, and the British Isles.

items.title: Conwy Castle
items.fact: Conwy Castle is a fortification in Conwy, located in North Wales. It was built by Edward I, during his conquest of Wales, between 1283 and 1287.

items.title: Snowdon
items.fact: Snowdon, or Yr Wyddfa, is a mountain in Snowdonia in North Wales.

items.title: Caernarfon Castle
items.fact: Caernarfon Castle is a medieval fortress in Gwynedd, north-west Wales.

items.title: The Rock of Cashel
items.fact: The Rock of Cashel, also known as Cashel of the Kings and St. Patrick's Rock, is a historical site located dramatically above a plain at Cashel, County Tipperary, Ireland.

items.title: Blarney Castle
items.fact: Blarney Castle is a medieval stronghold in Blarney, a town in Cork, Ireland.

items.title: Trinity College Dublin
items.fact: The College of the Holy and Undivided Trinity of Queen Elizabeth near Dublin, branded by the board as Trinity College, the University of Dublin.

items.title: Kilmainham Gaol
items.fact: Kilmainham Gaol is a former prison in Kilmainham, Dublin. Opened in the late 18th century as the County of Dublin Gaol, it is now a museum run by the Office of Public Works.

items.title: The Ring of Kerry
items.credit: Robert Linsdell  from St. Andrews, Canada
items.fact: The Ring of Kerry is a 179-kilometre-long circular tourist route in County Kerry, south-western Ireland.

items.title: Dunluce Castle
items.fact: Dunluce Castle is a now-ruined medieval castle in Northern Ireland, the seat of Clan MacQuillan.

items.title: Portmeirion
items.fact: Portmeirion is a folly Italianate style tourist village in Gwynedd, North Wales.

items.title: Tintern Abbey
items.fact: Tintern Abbey is a ruined medieval abbey adjacent to the village of Tintern in Monmouthshire, on the Welsh bank of the River Wye.

items.title: The Angel of the North
items.fact: The Angel of the North is a contemporary sculpture by Antony Gormley, located in Gateshead, Tyne and Wear, England.

items.title: The Louvre
items.fact: The Louvre is a national art museum in Paris, France.

items.title: Horseshoe Bend
items.fact: Horseshoe Bend is a horseshoe-shaped incised meander of the Colorado River located near the town of Page, Arizona, United States.

items.title: Antelope Canyon
items.fact: Navajo Upper Antelope Canyon is a slot canyon in the American Southwest, on Navajo land east of Lechee, Arizona.

items.title: Zion Canyon
items.fact: Zion National Park is a national park of the United States located in southwestern Utah near the town of Springdale.

items.title: Arches National Park
items.fact: Arches National Park is a national park of the United States in eastern Utah. The park is adjacent to the Colorado River, 4 mi north of Moab, Utah.

items.title: Devils Tower
items.fact: Devils Tower is a laccolithic butte, composed of igneous rock in the Bear Lodge Ranger District of the Black Hills, near Hulett and Sundance in Crook County, northeastern Wyoming.

items.title: The Grand Prismatic Spring
items.fact: The Grand Prismatic Spring is the largest hot spring in the Yellowstone National Park, and the third largest in the world, after Frying Pan Lake in New Zealand and Boiling Lake in Dominica.

items.title: Glacier National Park
items.fact: Glacier National Park is a national park of the United States located in northwestern Montana, on the Canada–United States border.

items.title: Mount Rainier
items.fact: Mount Rainier, also known as Tahoma, is a large, active stratovolcano in the Cascade Range of the Pacific Northwest in the United States.

items.title: Multnomah Falls
items.credit: John Fowler  from Placitas, NM, USA
items.fact: Multnomah Falls is a waterfall located on Multnomah Creek in the Columbia River Gorge, east of Troutdale, between Corbett and Dodson, Oregon, United States.

items.title: The Santa Monica Pier
items.fact: The Santa Monica Pier is a large pier at the foot of Colorado Avenue in Santa Monica, California, United States.

items.title: Lake Tahoe
items.fact: Lake Tahoe is a freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada of the Western United States, straddling the border between California and Nevada.

items.title: The Redwoods
items.fact: The Redwood National and State Parks are a complex of one United States national park and three California state parks located along the coast of northern California.

items.title: Denali
items.fact: Denali, federally designated as Mount McKinley, is the highest mountain peak in North America, with a summit elevation of 20,310 feet above sea level.

items.title: The Mendenhall Glacier
items.fact: Mendenhall Glacier is a glacier about 13.6 miles long located in Mendenhall Valley, about 12 miles from downtown Juneau in the southeast area of the U.S. state of Alaska.

items.title: Waikiki Beach
items.fact: Waikīkī is a Honolulu neighborhood and the eponymous Waikīkī beach on its south shore, on the island of Oʻahu in the U.S. state of Hawaii.

items.title: Diamond Head
items.fact: Diamond Head is a volcanic tuff cone on the Hawaiian island of Oʻahu.

items.title: The Kilauea volcano
items.fact: Kīlauea is an active shield volcano in the Hawaiian Islands, located along the southeastern shore of Hawaii Island.

items.title: The Banff Springs Hotel
items.fact: The Fairmont Banff Springs, formerly and commonly known as the Banff Springs Hotel, is a historic hotel in western Canada, located in Banff, Alberta.

items.title: Moraine Lake
items.fact: Moraine Lake is a snow and glacially fed alpine lake in Banff National Park, 14 kilometres outside the village of Lake Louise, Alberta, Canada.

items.title: Parliament Hill
items.fact: Parliament Hill is an area of Crown land on the southern bank of the Ottawa River that houses the Parliament of Canada in downtown Ottawa, Ontario.

items.title: Peggy's Cove
items.fact: Peggys Cove is a small rural community located on the eastern shore of St. Margarets Bay in the Halifax Regional Municipality.

items.title: Teotihuacan
items.fact: Teotihuacan is an ancient Mesoamerican city located in a sub-valley of the Valley of Mexico, which is located in the State of Mexico, 40 kilometers northeast of modern-day Mexico City.

items.title: Tulum
items.fact: Tulum is the site of a pre-Columbian Mayan walled city which served as a major port for Coba, in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo.

items.title: The Palacio de Bellas Artes
items.fact: The Palacio de Bellas Artes is a prominent cultural center in Mexico City. It hosts performing arts events, literature events and plastic arts galleries and exhibitions.

items.title: The Galápagos Islands
items.fact: The Galápagos Islands are an archipelago of volcanic islands in the Eastern Pacific, located around the equator, 485 nautical miles west of the mainland of South America.

items.title: The Nazca Lines
items.fact: The Nazca lines are a group of geoglyphs made in the soil of the Nazca Desert in southern Peru.

items.title: Rainbow Mountain
items.fact: Vinicunca, or Winikunka, also called Montaña de Siete Colores, Montaña de Colores, or Montaña Arcoíris, is a mountain in the Andes of Peru with an altitude of 5,036 metres above sea level.

items.title: Perito Moreno Glacier
items.fact: The Perito Moreno, Francisco Gormaz or Bismarck Glacier is a glacier located in Los Glaciares National Park in southwest Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.

items.title: The Copacabana
items.fact: Copacabana is a Brazilian bairro located in the South Zone of the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

items.title: Sugarloaf Mountain
items.fact: Sugarloaf Mountain is a peak situated in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on a peninsula at the mouth of Guanabara Bay.

items.title: The Palace of Versailles
items.fact: The Palace of Versailles is a château and historic monument in Versailles in the Yvelines department of France, southwest of Paris.

items.title: Mont Blanc
items.fact: Mont Blanc is a mountain in the Alps, rising 4,807.3 m above sea level, located right at the Franco-Italian border.

items.title: The Pont du Gard
items.fact: The Pont du Gard is an ancient Roman aqueduct bridge built in the first century AD to carry water over 50 km to the Roman colony of Nemausus.

items.title: Chambord
items.fact: The Château de Chambord in Chambord, Centre-Val de Loire, France, is one of the most recognisable châteaux in the world because of its very distinctive French Renaissance architecture.

items.title: Carcassonne
items.fact: The Cité de Carcassonne is a medieval citadel located in the French city of Carcassonne, in the Aude department, Occitania region.

items.title: The Palais Garnier
items.fact: The Palais Garnier, also known as Opéra Garnier, is a historic 1,979-seat opera house at the Place de l'Opéra in the 9th arrondissement of Paris, France.

items.title: Chartres Cathedral
items.fact: Chartres Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in Chartres, France, about 80 km southwest of Paris, and is the seat of the Bishop of Chartres.

items.title: The Atomium
items.fact: The Atomium is a landmark modernist building in Brussels, Belgium, originally constructed as the centrepiece of the 1958 Brussels World's Fair.

items.title: Bruges
items.fact: Bruges is the capital and largest city of the province of West Flanders, in the Flemish Region of Belgium.

items.title: The Rijksmuseum
items.fact: The Rijksmuseum is the national museum of the Netherlands dedicated to Dutch arts and history, located at the Museum Square in the borough of Amsterdam South, close to the Van Gogh Museum.

items.title: The Keukenhof
items.fact: Keukenhof, also known as the Garden of Europe, is one of the world's largest flower gardens, situated in the municipality of Lisse, in the Netherlands.

items.title: Anne Frank House
items.fact: The Anne Frank House is a writer's house and biographical museum dedicated to Jewish wartime diarist Anne Frank.

items.title: The Aqueduct of Segovia
items.fact: The Aqueduct of Segovia is a Roman aqueduct in Spain, built around the first century AD to channel water from springs in the mountains 17 kilometres to Segovia's fountains.

items.title: The Guggenheim Bilbao
items.fact: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is a museum of modern and contemporary art in Bilbao, Biscay, Spain.

items.title: Park Güell
items.fact: Park Güell is a complex of parks and gardens in Barcelona with architectural elements, located in the La Salut neighborhood of the Gràcia district in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

items.title: The Mezquita of Córdoba
items.fact: The Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba is the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Córdoba in the Spanish region of Andalusia.

items.title: Santiago de Compostela Cathedral
items.fact: Santiago de Compostela Cathedral is the end of the Camino, the pilgrim route walked across northern Spain for more than a thousand years.

items.title: Belém Tower
items.fact: Belém Tower, officially the Tower of Saint Vincent, is a 16th-century fortification located in Lisbon, Portugal.

items.title: Pena Palace
items.fact: The Pena Palace is a Romanticist palace in São Pedro de Penaferrim, in the municipality of Sintra, on the Portuguese Riviera.
items.place: Sintra (Santa Maria e São Miguel, São Martinho e São Pedro de Penaferrim), Portugal

items.title: The Douro Valley
items.credit: Vitor Oliveira  from Torres Vedras, PORTUGAL
items.fact: The Douro is the largest river of the Iberian Peninsula by discharge.

items.title: Saint Mark's Basilica
items.fact: The Patriarchal Cathedral Basilica of Saint Mark, commonly known as St Mark's Basilica.

items.title: The Rialto Bridge
items.fact: The Rialto Bridge is the oldest of the four bridges spanning the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy.

items.title: The Duomo of Florence
items.fact: Florence Cathedral, formally the Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Flower, is the cathedral of the Catholic Archdiocese of Florence in Florence, Italy.

items.title: The Ponte Vecchio
items.fact: The Ponte Vecchio is a medieval stone closed-spandrel segmental arch bridge over the Arno, in Florence, Italy.

items.title: The Pantheon
items.fact: The Pantheon is an ancient temple in Rome, Italy, originally built under emperor Augustus and reconstructed under Hadrian; since AD 609, it is a Catholic church called the Basilica of St.

items.title: The Spanish Steps
items.fact: The Spanish Steps in Rome, Italy, climb a steep slope between the Piazza di Spagna at the base and the Piazza Trinità dei Monti, dominated by the Trinità dei Monti church, at the top.

items.title: Pompeii
items.fact: Pompeii was a city in what is now the municipality of Pompei, near Naples, in the Campania region of Italy.

items.title: Mount Vesuvius
items.fact: Mount Vesuvius is a somma–stratovolcano located on the Gulf of Naples in Campania, Italy, about 9 km east of Naples and a short distance from the shore.

items.title: The Amalfi Coast
items.fact: The Amalfi Coast is a stretch of coastline overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea and the Gulf of Salerno.

items.title: Cinque Terre
items.fact: The Cinque Terre is a coastal area within Liguria, in the northwest of Italy.

items.title: Lake Como
items.fact: Lake Como, also known as Lario, is a lake of glacial origin in Lombardy, Italy. It has an area of 146 km2, making it the third-largest lake in Italy, after Lake Garda and Lake Maggiore.

items.title: The Milan Cathedral
items.fact: Milan Cathedral, or Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica of the Nativity of Saint Mary, is the cathedral church of Milan, Lombardy, Italy. Dedicated to the Nativity of St.

items.title: Mount Etna
items.fact: Mount Etna, or simply Etna, is an active stratovolcano on the east coast of Sicily, Italy, in the Metropolitan City of Catania, between the cities of Messina and Catania.

items.title: Meteora
items.fact: Meteora is a rock formation in the regional unit of Trikala, in Thessaly, in northwestern Greece, hosting one of the most prominent complexes of Eastern Orthodox monasteries.

items.title: The Temple of Poseidon
items.fact: Cape Sounion is the promontory at the southernmost tip of the Attica peninsula, 8 kilometres south of the town of Lavrio, and 69.5 km southeast of Athens in the Athens Riviera.

items.title: Delphi
items.fact: Delphi, in legend previously called Pytho, was an ancient sacred precinct in central Greece.

items.title: Prague Castle
items.fact: Prague Castle is a castle complex in Prague, Czech Republic serving as the official residence and workplace of the president of the Czech Republic.

items.title: The Cologne Cathedral
items.fact: Cologne Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in Cologne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is the seat of the Archbishop of Cologne and of the administration of the Archdiocese of Cologne.

items.title: The Berlin Wall
items.fact: The Berlin Wall was a guarded concrete barrier that encircled West Berlin from 1961 to 1989, separating it from East Berlin and the German Democratic Republic.

items.title: The Zugspitze
items.fact: The Zugspitze, at 2,962 m above sea level, is the highest peak of the Wetterstein Mountains and the highest mountain in Germany.

items.title: Schönbrunn Palace
items.fact: Schönbrunn Palace was the main summer residence of the Habsburg rulers, located in Hietzing, the 13th district of Vienna.

items.title: Hallstatt
items.fact: Hallstatt is a small town in the Gmunden District of the Austrian state of Upper Austria.

items.title: Chora Church
items.fact: The Chora Church or Kariye Mosque (Turkish: Kariye Camii) was a Byzantine church, now converted to a mosque (for the second time), in the Edirnekapı neighborhood of Fatih district, Istanbul, Turkey. It is famous for its outstanding Late Byzantine mosaics and frescos.

items.fact: The High Cathedral of Saint Peter in Trier (German: Hohe Domkirche St. Peter zu Trier), or Trier Cathedral (German: Trierer Dom), is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Trier, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany.

items.fact: The Basilica of San Lorenzo Maggiore is a Roman Catholic church in Milan, Northern Italy. Located within the city's ring of navigli, it is one of the oldest churches in the city, originally built in Roman times, but subsequently rebuilt several times over the centuries.

items.title: Ulm Minster
items.fact: Ulm Minster (German: Ulmer Münster) is a Gothic church of the Evangelical Church in Germany located in Ulm, Baden-Württemberg. It is the second-tallest church building in the world, with a steeple measuring 161.53 metres (530.0 ft).

items.title: Sacré-Cœur
items.fact: The Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Montmartre (French: Basilique du Sacré-Cœur de Montmartre), commonly known as Sacré-Cœur Basilica (French: Basilique du Sacré-Cœur) or simply Sacré-Cœur (French: Sacré-Cœur, pronounced [sakre kœr]), is a Catholic church and minor basilica in Paris dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

items.title: Helsinki Cathedral
items.fact: Helsinki Cathedral (Finnish: Helsingin tuomiokirkko, Suurkirkko; Swedish: Helsingfors domkyrka, Storkyrkan) is the Finnish Evangelical Lutheran cathedral of the Diocese of Helsinki, located in the neighborhood of Kruununhaka in the centre of Helsinki, Finland, at the Senate Square.

items.title: Geghard

items.title: Panthéon
items.fact: The Panthéon (French: [pɑ̃.te.ɔ̃] , from Ancient Greek πάνθειον (pántheion) '[temple] to all the gods') is a monument in the 5th arrondissement of Paris, France. items.title: Church of Saint-Sulpice
items.fact: The Church of Saint-Sulpice (French pronunciation: [sɛ̃ sylpis] ) is a Catholic church in Paris, France, on the east side of Place Saint-Sulpice, in the 6th arrondissement. It is the second largest church in the city.

items.title: Notre Dame du Haut

items.fact: The church of Saint Mary at Mount Naranco (Spanish: Iglesia de Santa María del Naranco; Asturian: Ilesia de Santa María'l Narancu) is a pre-Romanesque Asturian building on the slope of Mount Naranco situated 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) from Oviedo, northern Spain.

items.fact: The Sanctuary of Las Lajas (in full Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Holy Rosary of Las Lajas) is a Catholic minor basilica located within the canyon of the Guáitara River in Ipiales, Nariño Department, Colombia. items.title: Temple Church, London
items.fact: The Temple Church, a royal peculiar in the Church of England, is a church in the Inner and Middle Temples located between Fleet Street and the River Thames in London, England. items.title: Trinità dei Monti
items.fact: The Church of Santissima Trinità dei Monti, often called simply Trinità dei Monti (French: La Trinité-des-Monts), is a Roman Catholic late Renaissance titular church, part of a monastery complex in Rome. items.title: Turku Cathedral
items.fact: Turku Cathedral (Finnish: Turun tuomiokirkko, Swedish: Åbo domkyrka) is the only medieval basilica in Finland and the Mother Church of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Finland. items.fact: The Westerkerk (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈʋɛstərˌkɛr(ə)k]; English: Western Church) is a Reformed church within Dutch Protestant Calvinism in central Amsterdam, Netherlands. items.title: Hagia Sophia, Trabzon

items.fact: San Giorgio Maggiore (San Zorzi Mazor in Venetian) is a 16th-century Benedictine church on the island of the same name in Venice, northern Italy, designed by Andrea Palladio, and built between 1566 and 1610.

items.title: Sant'Andrea della Valle

items.fact: The Oude Kerk (Old Church), nicknamed Oude Jan ("Old John") and Scheve Jan ("Skewed John"), is a Gothic Protestant church in the old city centre of Delft, the Netherlands. Its most recognisable feature is a 75-metre-high brick tower that leans about two metres from the vertical.

items.title: Chiesa di San Cataldo
items.fact: The Church of San Cataldo (or Saint Cathal's Church) is a Catholic church located at Piazza Bellini, in central Palermo, Sicily, Italy. items.title: Vittskövle Church
items.fact: Vittskövle Church (Swedish: Vittskövle kyrka) is a church in Kristianstad Municipality, in Skåne, Sweden. It is part of the Diocese of Lund.

items.title: King's Mosque in Pristina
items.fact: The Imperial Mosque, also known as King's Mosque, is an Ottoman mosque located in Pristina, Kosovo. It was built in 1461 by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror.

items.title: Saint-Gervais-Saint-Protais
items.fact: Saint-Gervais-Saint-Protais (French pronunciation: [sɛ̃ ʒɛʁvɛ sɛ̃ pʁɔtɛ]) is a Roman Catholic parish church located in the 4th arrondissement of Paris, on Place Saint-Gervais in the Marais district, east of City Hall (Hôtel de Ville).

items.title: Malmesbury Abbey
items.fact: Malmesbury Abbey, at Malmesbury in Wiltshire, England, is a former Benedictine abbey dedicated to Saint Peter and Saint Paul. It was one of the few English religious houses with a continuous history from the 7th century through to the Dissolution of the Monasteries.

items.title: Kvetera Church
items.fact: Kvetera Church (Georgian: კვეტერის ეკლესია, romanized: k'vet'eris ek'lesia) is a Georgian Orthodox church in a historic fortified town of Kvetera in Kakheti. Kvetera Church was built in the early part of the 10th century.

items.title: Alphabetic Tower
items.fact: The Alphabetic Tower (Georgian: ანბანის კოშკი, romanized: anbanis k'oshk'i) is a 130-meter-high structure in Batumi, Georgia. The tower symbolizes the uniqueness of the Georgian alphabet and people.

items.title: Friedrichswerder Church
items.fact: Friedrichswerder Church (German: Friedrichswerdersche Kirche, French: Temple du Werder) was the first Neo-Gothic church built in Berlin, Germany. It was designed by an architect better known for his Neoclassical architecture, Karl Friedrich Schinkel, and was built under his direction from 1824 to 1831.

items.title: Church of the Multiplication
items.fact: The Church of the Multiplication of the Loaves and Fish (Latin: Ecclesia multiplicationis panum et piscium), shortened to the Church of the Multiplication, is a Roman Catholic church located at Tabgha, on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee in Israel. The modern church rests on the site of two earlier churches.

items.title: Chapel of the Resurrection, Brussels
items.fact: The Chapel of the Resurrection (French: Chapelle de la Résurrection; Dutch: Verrijzeniskapel), or the Chapel for Europe (French: Chapelle pour l'Europe; Dutch: Europakapel), is a Catholic church with an ecumenical vocation located in the heart of the Brussels' European Quarter (City of Brussels municipality), next to the former Convent Van Maerlant.

items.title: San Salvador
items.fact: The Church of Santissimo Salvatore (Italian: Chiesa del Santissimo Salvatore, lit. 'Church of the Most Holy Saviour'), usually known by its Venetian name of San Salvador, is a church in Venice, northern Italy.

items.title: Church of the Transfiguration
items.fact: The Church of the Transfiguration (Arabic: كنيسة التجلي, romanized: Kanīsat At-tajalli, Hebrew: כנסיית ההשתנות) is a Franciscan church located on Mount Tabor in Israel.

items.title: Church of the Acheiropoietos
items.fact: The Church of the Acheiropoietos (Greek: [Παναγία] Ἀχειροποίητος) is a 5th-century Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church, located in the city of Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, in northern Greece. It is situated in the city's centre, at Agias Sofias street opposite Makedonomachon square.

items.title: Panagia Ekatontapiliani church
items.fact: Panagia Ekatontapiliani (Greek: Παναγία η Εκατονταπυλιανή); literally the church with 100 gates) or Panagia Katapoliani (Greek: Παναγία η Καταπολιανή) is a historic Byzantine church complex in Parikia town, on the island of Paros in Greece.

items.title: San Giovanni a Porta Latina
items.fact: San Giovanni a Porta Latina (Italian: "Saint John Before the Latin Gate") is a basilica church in Rome, Italy, near the Porta Latina (on the Via Latina) of the Aurelian Wall.

items.title: Sant'Andrea delle Fratte
items.fact: Sant'Andrea delle Fratte ("Saint Andrew of the Thickets") is a 17th-century basilica church in Rome, Italy, dedicated to St. Andrew.

items.title: Iglesia de la Concepción
items.fact: The Iglesia-Parroquia Matriz de Nuestra Señora de La Concepción (Church of the Immaculate Conception) is a Roman Catholic church located in the city of San Cristóbal de La Laguna (Canary Islands, Spain). This church is almost a twin of the Church of the Conception of Santa Cruz de Tenerife.

items.title: Kashveti Church
items.fact: The Kashveti Church of St. George (Georgian: ქაშვეთის წმინდა გიორგის სახელობის ტაძარი) is a Georgian Orthodox Church in central Tbilisi, located across from the Parliament building on Rustaveli Avenue.

items.title: St. Martin's Church
items.fact: The Church of St. Martin is a medieval church in Landshut, Bavaria.

items.title: Madonna dell'Orto
items.fact: The Madonna dell'Orto is a church in Venice, Italy, in the sestiere of Cannaregio. This was the home parish of Tintoretto and holds a number of his works as well as his tomb.

items.title: Munttoren
items.credit: The original uploader was P.H. Louw at Dutch Wikipedia.
items.fact: The Munttoren (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈmʏnˌtoːrə(n)]; "Mint Tower") or Munt ([mʏnt]) is a tower in Amsterdam, Netherlands. It stands on the busy Muntplein square, where the Amstel river and the Singel canal meet, near the flower market and the eastern end of the Kalverstraat shopping street.

items.fact: St. Sebaldus Church (St.

items.title: Saint Wenceslas Cathedral
items.credit: Kirk, shifted & cropped by Rabanus Flavus
items.fact: Saint Wenceslas Cathedral (Czech: Katedrála svatého Václava) is a neogothic cathedral at Wenceslas Square in Olomouc, in the Czech Republic, founded in 1107. The square was named after Saint Wenceslaus I, Duke of Bohemia on the thousandth anniversary of his death in 935.

items.title: Basilika of St. Ludmila
items.fact: The Basilica of St. Ludmila (Czech: bazilika svaté Ludmily) is a Catholic church at the square Náměstí Míru in Vinohrady district of Prague, Czech Republic.

items.title: Périgueux Cathedral
items.fact: Périgueux Cathedral is a Catholic church located in the city of Périgueux, France. A cathedral since 1669, it is dedicated to Saint Front (French: Cathédrale Saint-Front de Périgueux).

items.title: San Francesco di Paola
items.fact: San Francesco di Paola is a prominent church located to the west in Piazza del Plebiscito, the main square of Naples, Italy. The construction started in 1816 and ended in 1846.

items.title: San Giorgio in Velabro
items.fact: San Giorgio in Velabro is a Catholic church dedicated to St. George on Via del Velabro in the historic center of Rome in the Velabrum and the Ripa district.

items.title: San Lorenzo in Damaso
items.fact: The Minor Basilica of St. Lawrence in Damaso (Basilica Minore di San Lorenzo in Damaso) or simply San Lorenzo in Damaso is a parish and titular church in central Rome, Italy that is dedicated to St.

items.title: San Marcello al Corso
items.fact: San Marcello al Corso is an ancient titular and conventual church in Rome, Italy. It has been served by friars of the Servite Order since c.

items.title: San Giovanni degli Eremiti
items.fact: San Giovanni degli Eremiti (St John of the Hermits) is an ancient former monastic church located on Via Benedettini #19 in the ancient quarter of Albergaria of the city of Palermo, region of Sicily, Italy. It is about two blocks south from the Palazzo dei Normanni, adjacent to the church of San Giorgio in Kemonia.

items.title: Sancaktar Hayrettin Mosque
items.fact: Sancaktar Hayrettin Mosque (Turkish: Sancaktar Hayrettin Câmîi; also Sancaktar Hayrettin Mescidi, where Mescit is the Turkish word for a small mosque, or Sancaktar Mescidi) is part of a former Eastern Orthodox monastery converted into a mosque by the Ottomans.

items.title: Santa Maria in Vallicella
items.credit: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please mention me as the author and send me a message. This image
items.fact: Santa Maria in Vallicella, also called Chiesa Nuova, is a church in Rome, Italy, which today faces onto the main thoroughfare of the Corso Vittorio Emanuele and the corner of Via della Chiesa Nuova.

items.title: Santa Pudenziana
items.fact: The Basilica of Santa Pudentiana is the eldest Roman Catholic basilica built in the fourth century in Rome. The original shrine building dates back from the second century and is dedicated to Saint Pudentiana, sister to Praxedes the martyress.

items.title: Santa Susanna
items.fact: The Church of Saint Susanna at the Baths of Diocletian (Italian: Chiesa di Santa Susanna alle Terme di Diocleziano) is a Catholic parish and Cistercian conventual church located on the Quirinal Hill in Rome, Italy. There has been a titular church associated to its site as far back as AD 280.

items.title: Saint-Pierre de Montmartre
items.fact: Saint-Pierre de Montmartre (French pronunciation: [sɛ̃ pjɛr də mɔ̃martr]) is the second oldest surviving church in Paris, after the Abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Pres. It is one of the two main churches on Montmartre, the other being the more famous 19th-century Sacré-Cœur Basilica, just above it.

items.title: Peace Church in Świdnica
items.fact: The Holy Trinity Church of Peace in Świdnica is the largest wooden Baroque temple in Europe and a historic religious building built under the agreements of the Treaty of Westphalia signed in 1648, which ended the Thirty Years' War. It belongs to the Świdnica parish of the Evangelical-Augsburg Church in Poland.

items.title: Torre dei Conti
items.fact: The Torre dei Conti is a medieval fortified tower in Rome, Italy, located near the Colosseum and the Roman Forum.

items.title: San Crisogono
items.fact: Basilica di San Crisogono (English: Basilica of Saint Chrysogonos) is a titular church and minor basilica located in Trastevere, Rome. Established in the 4th century under Pope Sylvester I, it is one of the oldest parish churches in the city and has served as a cardinal titular church since early Christianity.

items.title: German Church
items.fact: The German Church (German: Deutsche Kirche [ˈdɔʏtʃə kɪʁçə]; Swedish: Tyska kyrkan [ˈtʏ̌sːka ˈɕʏ̂rːkan]), sometimes called St. Gertrude's Church (Swedish: Sankta Gertruds kyrka), is a church in Gamla stan, the old town in central Stockholm, Sweden, belonging to the German Saint Gertrude Parish of the Church of Sweden.

items.title: Frauenkirche
items.fact: The Frauenkirche ("Church of Our Lady") is a church in Nuremberg, Germany. It stands on the eastern side of the main market.

items.title: Mantua Cathedral
items.fact: Mantua Cathedral (Italian: Cattedrale di San Pietro apostolo; Duomo di Mantova) in Mantua, Lombardy, northern Italy, is a Roman Catholic cathedral dedicated to Saint Peter. It is the seat of the Bishop of Mantua.

items.title: Abbazia di Pomposa
items.fact: Pomposa Abbey is a Benedictine monastery in the comune of Codigoro on the Adriatic coast near Ferrara, Italy. It was one of the most important monasteries in the northern Italy and is famous for the Carolingian manuscripts preserved in its rich library, one of the wealthiest of Carolingian repositories, and for the Romanesque buildings.

items.title: Ateni Sioni Church
items.fact: The Ateni Sioni Church (Georgian: ატენის სიონი) is an early 7th-century Georgian Orthodox church in the village of Ateni, some 10 km (6.2 mi) south of the city of Gori, Georgia. It stands in a setting of Ateni gorge in the Tana River valley known not only for its historical monuments, but also for its picturesque landscapes and wine.

items.title: Basilica di Sant'Anastasia al Palatino
items.fact: Sant'Anastasia is a minor basilica and titular church for cardinal-priests in Rome, Italy managed by the Syro-Malabar Catholic Church.

items.title: Sanctuary of the Madonna di San Luca
items.fact: The Sanctuary of the Madonna of San Luca is a basilica church located in Bologna, northern Italy, situated atop the forested hill of Colle (or Monte) della Guardia, approximately 300 metres above the city plain, just southwest of the historical centre.

items.title: Michael's Gate
items.fact: In Bratislava, Slovakia, Michael's Gate (Slovak: Michalská brána, German: Michaelertor, Hungarian: Mihály kapu) is the only city gate that has been preserved of the medieval fortifications and ranks among the oldest town buildings in Bratislava, Slovakia.

items.title: Rozhen Monastery
items.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Reinhard P. Braun~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims).
items.fact: The Rozhen Monastery of the Nativity of the Mother of God (Bulgarian: Роженски манастир "Рождество Богородично", Rozhenski manastir "Rozhdestvo Bogorodichno", Greek: Μονή Ροζινού, Moni Rozinou) is the biggest monastery in the Pirin Mountains in southwestern Bulgaria, nestled in the Melnik Earth Pyramids.

items.title: Santa Maria in Campitelli
items.fact: Santa Maria in Campitelli or Santa Maria in Portico (Santa Maria in Portico di Campitelli) is a church dedicated to the Virgin Mary on the narrow Piazza di Campitelli in Rione Sant'Angelo, Rome, Italy. The church is served by the Clerics Regular of the Mother of God.

items.title: Santo Stefano, Venice
items.fact: The Chiesa di Santo Stefano (Church of St. Stephen) is a large Roman Catholic church at the northern end of the Campo Santo Stefano in the sestiere of San Marco, Venice, Italy.

items.title: Santa Maria degli Scalzi
items.credit: Tony Hisgett, edited by MenkinAlRire (upright, centered, col.aberration, sharpness, brightness)
items.fact: Santa Maria di Nazareth is a Roman Catholic Carmelite church in Venice, northern Italy. It is also called Church of the Scalzi (Italian: Chiesa degli Scalzi) being the seat in the city of the Discalced Carmelites religious order (Scalzi in Italian means 'barefoot').

items.title: Church of Panaghia Kapnikarea
items.fact: The Church of Panagia Kapnikarea (Greek: Εκκλησία της Παναγίας Καπνικαρέας) or just Kapnikarea (Greek: Καπνικαρέα) is a Greek Orthodox church and one of the oldest continuously in use churches in Athens.

items.title: Church of St. Peter in Gallicantu
items.fact: Church of Saint Peter in Gallicantu is a Roman Catholic church located on the eastern slope of Mount Zion, just outside the walled Old City of Jerusalem. It is dedicated to the episode from the New Testament known as the Denial of Peter.

items.title: Church of Colònia Güell
items.fact: The Church of Colònia Güell (Catalan: Cripta de la Colònia Güell, IPA: [ˈkɾiptə ðə lə kuˈlɔniə ˈɣweʎ]) is an unfinished work by Antoni Gaudí. It was built as a place of worship for the people on a hillside in the namesake company town in Santa Coloma de Cervelló, near Barcelona (Catalonia, Spain).

items.title: Kreuzkirche
items.fact: The Dresden Kreuzkirche (Church of the Holy Cross) is a Lutheran church in Dresden, Germany. It is the main church and seat of the Landesbischof of the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of Saxony, and the largest church building in the Free State of Saxony.

items.title: Saint-Nicolas-du-Chardonnet
items.fact: Saint-Nicolas du Chardonnet (French pronunciation: [sɛ̃ ni.kɔ.lɑ dy ʃaʁ.dɔ.nɛ]) is a SSPX-occupied Catholic church in the centre of Paris, France, in the 5th arrondissement. It was constructed between 1656 and 1763.

items.title: San Miguel de Lillo
items.fact: St. Michael of Lillo (Spanish: San Miguel de Lillo, Asturian: Samiguel de Lliño) is a Roman Catholic church built on the Naranco mount, near the Church of Santa María del Naranco in Asturias.

items.title: Jubilee Church
items.fact: The Jubilee Church, formally known as Chiesa di Dio Padre Misericordioso (Italian for "Church of God the Merciful Father"), is a Catholic church and community center in Tor Tre Teste in Rome. According to Richard Meier, its architect, it is "the crown jewel of the Vicariato di Roma's (Archdiocese of Rome) Millennium project" (p.

items.title: Church of the Assumption of Our Lady and Saint John the Baptist
items.fact: The Church of the Assumption of Our Lady and Saint John the Baptist (Czech: Kostel Nanebevzetí Panny Marie a svatého Jana Křtitele) is a Gothic and Baroque Gothic church north-east of Kutná Hora in the Czech Republic and is listed in the UNESCO World Heritage List together with the Church of St. Barbara and other monuments in Kutná Hora.

items.title: Lakewood Church
items.fact: Lakewood Church is an evangelical Pentecostal and Word of Faith megachurch located in Houston, Texas. It was formerly a Baptist church from 1959 until 1961, and a non-denominational Christian church from 1961 to 1979.

items.title: Santa Maria presso San Satiro
items.fact: Santa Maria presso San Satiro (Saint Mary near Saint Satyrus) is a church in Milan. The Italian Renaissance structure (1476–1482) houses the early medieval shrine to Satyrus, brother of Saint Ambrose.

items.fact: St. Lorenz (St.

items.title: Saint-Vincent-de-Paul church
items.fact: The Church of Saint-Vincent-de-Paul (French: Église Saint-Vincent-de-Paul, pronounced [eɡliz sɛ̃ vɛ̃sɑ̃ də pɔl]) is a church in the 10th arrondissement of Paris dedicated to Saint Vincent de Paul. It gives its name to the Quartier Saint-Vincent-de-Paul around it.

items.title: Church of the Most Sacred Heart of Our Lord
items.fact: The Church of the Most Sacred Heart of Our Lord (Czech: Kostel Nejsvětějšího Srdce Páně) is a Roman Catholic church at Jiřího z Poděbrad Square in Prague's Vinohrady district. It was built between 1929 and 1932 and designed by the Slovene architect Jože Plečnik.

items.title: San Francesco a Ripa
items.fact: San Francesco a Ripa is a church in Rome, Italy. It is dedicated to Francis of Assisi who once stayed at the adjacent convent.

items.title: San Moisè
items.fact: The Chiesa di San Moisè (or San Moisè Profeta) is a Baroque style, Roman Catholic church in Venice, northern Italy.

items.title: Santa Cristina de Lena
items.fact: St Christine of Lena (Spanish: Santa Cristina de Lena) is a Roman Catholic Asturian pre-Romanesque church in the Lena municipality of Spain, about 25 kilometres (16 mi) south of Oviedo, on an old Roman road that joined the lands of the plateau with Asturias.

items.title: Santa Maria dell'Anima
items.fact: Santa Maria dell'Anima (English: Our Lady of the Soul) is a church in central Rome, Italy, just west of the Piazza Navona and near the Santa Maria della Pace church. It was founded during the course of the 14th century by Dutch merchants, who at that time belonged to the Holy Roman Empire.

items.title: Santa Maria in Montesanto
items.fact: Santa Maria in Montesanto is a titular minor basilica church in Rome, in the Rione Campo Marzio, which stands in Piazza del Popolo, between Via del Corso and Via del Babuino. It is also known as the Church of the Artists (Chiesa degli artisti).

items.title: Santa Prisca
items.fact: Santa Prisca is a titular church of Rome, on the Aventine Hill, for Cardinal-priests. It is recorded as the Titulus Priscae in the acts of the 499 synod.

items.title: Saint Nicholas' Church
items.fact: St. Nicholas Church (Dutch: Sint-Niklaaskerk) is a Roman Catholic church, as well as one of the oldest and most prominent landmarks in Ghent, Belgium.

items.title: St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church
items.fact: The St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church, officially the St.

items.title: Beyazıt Tower
items.fact: Beyazıt Tower, also named Seraskier Tower, from the name of the Ottoman ministry of War, is an 85-metre-tall (279 ft) fire-watch tower located in the courtyard of Istanbul University's main campus (formerly Ottoman Ministry of War) on Beyazıt Square (known as the Forum Tauri in the Roman period) in Istanbul, Turkey.

items.title: Powder Tower
items.fact: The Powder Tower (Latvian: Pulvertornis) is situated in Riga, Latvia, and originally a part of the defensive system of the town. The current Powder Tower was built in 1650 and renovated in the years 1937 to 1940 when it was added to the structure of the Latvian War Museum.

items.title: Gesuati
items.fact: Santa Maria del Rosario (St. Mary of the Rosary), commonly known as I Gesuati, is an 18th-century Dominican church in the Sestiere of Dorsoduro, on the Giudecca canal in Venice, northern Italy.

items.title: Saint Joseph's Oratory
items.fact: Saint Joseph's Oratory of Mount Royal (French: Oratoire Saint-Joseph-du-Mont-Royal) is a Roman Catholic minor basilica and national shrine located at 3800 Queen Mary Road in the Côte-des-Neiges neighborhood on Mount Royal's Westmount Summit in Montreal, Quebec.

items.title: San Sisto Vecchio
items.fact: The Basilica of San Sisto Vecchio (in Via Appia) is a Catholic minor basilica and Dominican conventual church in Rome, Italy. It has been a titular church since 600 AD.

items.title: Church of Our Lady of Laeken
items.fact: The Church of Our Lady of Laeken (French: Église Notre-Dame de Laeken; Dutch: Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk van Laken) is a Catholic parish church in the Brussels district of Laeken, Belgium.

items.title: Saint-Séverin
items.fact: The Church of Saint-Séverin (French: Église Saint-Séverin, pronounced [eɡliz sɛ̃ sevʁɛ̃]) is a Catholic church in the 5th arrondissement, or Latin Quarter, of Paris, on the lively tourist street Rue Saint-Séverin.

items.title: Grote Kerk
items.fact: The Grote Kerk or St.-Bavokerk is a Reformed Protestant church located on the central market square (Grote Markt) in the Dutch city of Haarlem. The church was built in 1307.

items.title: San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro
items.fact: The Basilica of St. Peter in the Golden Sky (Italian: Basilica di San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro) is an 8th-century Catholic basilica and monastery church served for centuries by the Augustinian friars in Pavia, in the Lombardy region of Italy.

items.title: Augustinian Church
items.fact: The Augustinian Church (German: Augustinerkirche) in Vienna is a parish church located on Josefsplatz, next to the Hofburg, the winter palace of the Habsburg dynasty in Vienna. Originally built in the 14th century as the parish church of the imperial court of the Habsburgs, the harmonious Gothic interior was added in the 18th century.

items.title: San Martino ai Monti
items.fact: San Martino ai Monti, officially known as Santi Silvestro e Martino ai Monti ("Saints Sylvester & Martin in the Mountains"), is a minor basilica in Rome, Italy, in the Rione Monti neighbourhood.

items.title: Mariatrost Basilica
items.fact: The Baroque Mariatrost Basilica on top of the Purberg hill in Mariatrost, a district of Graz, is one of the most famous pilgrimage sites of Styria in Austria. The pilgrimage church stands prominently on top of the Purberg hill (469 m) in the northeast of Graz.

items.title: Bologna Cathedral
items.fact: Bologna Cathedral, formally known as the Metropolitan Cathedral of Saint Peter (Italian: Cattedrale Metropolitana di San Pietro, also called Cattedrale di Bologna), is the cathedral of Bologna, Italy, and the seat of the Archbishop of Bologna.

items.title: Sant'Atanasio
items.fact: The Church of Saint Athanasius (Italian: Sant’Atanasio, Latin: S. Athanasii), also known as Sant'Atanasio dei Greci (Greek: Εκκλησία Αγίου Αθανασίου των Ελλήνων, Ekklisia Agiou Athanasiou ton Ellinon), is a Greek Catholic titular church located on Via del Babuino 149, near the Spanish Steps, in the rione Campo Marzio of Rome, Italy.

items.title: San Giovanni in Bragora
items.fact: San Giovanni in Bragora is a church in Venice, Italy, located in the sestiere of Castello.

items.title: Duomo di Pienza
items.fact: Pienza Cathedral (Italian: Duomo di Pienza; Concattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta) is a Roman Catholic cathedral dedicated to the Assumption of the Virgin Mary in Pienza, in the province of Siena, Italy.

items.title: Wooden articular church of Hronsek
items.fact: Wooden articular church of Hronsek is a Lutheran church situated in the village of Hronsek, in Slovakia.

items.title: Eidsborg Stave Church
items.fact: Eidsborg Stave Church (Norwegian: Eidsborg stavkyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tokke Municipality in Telemark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Eidsborg.

items.title: Santa Maria della Spina
items.fact: Santa Maria della Spina is a small church in the Italian city of Pisa. The church, erected around 1230 in the Pisan Gothic style, and enlarged after 1325, was originally known as Santa Maria di Pontenovo for the newer bridge that existed nearby, collapsed in the 15th century, and was never rebuilt.

items.title: Saint Peter's Church, Malmo
items.fact: Saint Peter's Church (Swedish: Sankt Petri kyrka) is a Brick Gothic church in Malmö, Sweden. Built in the 14th century as the main church of the city, it has been described as "the main Gothic monument within church architecture in Scania".

items.title: Christ Church, Windhoek
items.fact: The Christ Church (German: Christuskirche) is a historic landmark and Lutheran church in Windhoek, Namibia, belonging to the German-speaking Evangelical Lutheran Church in Namibia. It was designed by architect Gottlieb Redecker.

items.title: Candelária Church
items.fact: The Candelária Church (Portuguese: Igreja da Candelária, pronounced [iˈgɾeʒɐ ðɐ kɐ̃deˈlaɾjɐ]) is an important historical Roman Catholic church in the city of Rio de Janeiro, in southeastern Brazil. It was built and decorated during a long period, from 1775 to the late 19th century.

items.title: Clérigos Church
items.fact: The Clérigos Church (Portuguese: Igreja dos Clérigos, pronounced [ˈklɛɾiɣuʃ]; "Church of the Clergymen") is a Baroque church in the city of Porto, in Portugal. Its 75-meter-tall bell tower, the Torre dos Clérigos, can be seen from various points of the city and is one of its most characteristic symbols.

items.title: St. Stephen's Basilica, Jerusalem
items.fact: The St. Stephen's Basilica (Hebrew: מנזר סנט אטיין) or simply the Church of St.

items.title: Santissimo Nome di Maria al Foro Traiano
items.fact: The Church of the Most Holy Name of Mary at the Trajan Forum (Italian: Santissimo Nome di Maria al Foro Traiano, Latin: Ss. Nominis Mariae ad forum Traiani) is a Roman Catholic church in Rome, Italy.

items.title: Skałka
items.fact: The Church of St. Michael the Archangel and St.

items.title: Town Hall Tower
items.fact: Town Hall Tower (Polish: Wieża ratuszowa) is one of the main focal points of the Main Market Square in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland. The Tower is the only remaining part of the old Kraków Town Hall, demolished in 1820 as part of the city plan to open up the Main Square.

items.title: St. Pantaleon's Church
items.fact: The Church of Saint Pantaleon (German: Sankt Pantaleon [ˌzaŋkt panˈtaːleɔn]; Kölsch: Zint Pantalejon [ˌtsɪ̂nt panˈtálɪjɔn]) is an early Romanesque church in Cologne, Germany. The church dates back to the 10th century and is one of the twelve Romanesque churches of Cologne.

items.title: Cattolica di Stilo
items.fact: The Cattolica di Stilo is a Byzantine church in the comune of Stilo (Province of Reggio), Calabria, southern Italy. It is a national monument, and part of the "Evidence of Italo-Greek Culture between the Early and Late Middle Ages" proposed World Heritage Site.

items.title: Church of Hosios David
items.fact: The Church of Hosios David (Greek: Όσιος Δαυίδ) is a late 5th-century church in Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of Greece.

items.title: St Paul's Pro-Cathedral
items.fact: St Paul's Pro-Cathedral (Malti: Il-Pro-Katridral ta' San Pawl), officially The Pro-Cathedral and Collegiate Church of Saint Paul, is an Anglican pro-cathedral of the Diocese in Europe situated in Independence Square, Valletta, Malta. A "pro-cathedral" is a church with cathedral status though not being the main cathedral.

items.title: Omar Khayyam Mausoleum
items.fact: The Mausoleum of Omar Khayyám (Persian: آرامگاه عمر خیام); is a mausoleum of white marble erected over Omar Khayyám's headstone, located on the south-east of the city of Nishapur, in the northeastern province of Razavi Khorasan, Iran. The mausoleum is a symbol of contemporary Iranian architecture.

items.title: St Paul's Archcathedral
items.fact: St Paul's Cathedral is a cathedral in Tirana, Albania. It belongs to the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Tiranë-Durrës.

items.title: Căpriana monastery
items.fact: The Căpriana Monastery (Romanian: Mănăstirea Căpriana) is one of the oldest monasteries of Moldova, located in Căpriana, 40 km (25 miles) north-west of Chișinău.

items.title: Stroganov Church
items.fact: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary (Russian: Церковь Собора Пресвятой Богородицы), better known as Nativity or Stroganov is a Russian Orthodox church, located at the Rozhdestvenskaya Street in Nizhny Novgorod. It was built in 1696–1719 on the means of the merchant Grigory Stroganov.

items.title: Oulu Cathedral
items.fact: Oulu Cathedral (Finnish: Oulun tuomiokirkko, Swedish: Uleåborgs domkyrka) is an Evangelical Lutheran cathedral and the seat of the Diocese of Oulu, located in the center of Oulu, Finland. The church was built in 1777 as a tribute to the king of Sweden Gustav III and named after his wife as Sofia Magdalena's church.

items.title: San Sebastiano
items.fact: The Temple of San Sebastiano is a late-Renaissance- or Mannerist-style church in central Milan. The cylindrical church is shaped like a can capped with a dome.

items.title: Sant'Agata dei Goti Church
items.fact: Sant'Agata dei Goti is a titular church in Rome, Italy, dedicated to the martyr Agatha of Sicily and the home of the Congregation of the Sacred Stigmata’s (Stigmatines) General Curia. The diaconia is assigned to Cardinal Raymond Leo Burke, patron emeritus of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta.

items.title: Santa Maria Formosa
items.fact: Santa Maria Formosa, formally The Church of the Purification of Mary, is a church in Venice, northern Italy. It was erected in 1492 under the design by Renaissance architect Mauro Codussi.

items.title: Svanetian tower
items.fact: Svan towers (Georgian: სვანური კოშკი, romanized: svanuri k'oshk'i) refers to the tower houses built as defensive dwellings in the Georgian historical region of Svaneti (present-day Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti). These towers are unique to the region and were primarily built between the 9th and 12th centuries, during the Georgian Golden Age.

items.fact: The Torre del Mangia is a tower in Siena, in the Tuscany region of Italy. Built in 1338–1348, it is located in the Piazza del Campo, Siena's main square, next to the Palazzo Pubblico (Town Hall).

items.title: Church of Saint Panteleimon
items.fact: The Church of Saint Panteleimon (Greek: Ναός Αγίου Παντελεήμονα, romanized: Naós Agíou Panteleímona), officially the Holy Church of Saint Panteleimon (Ιερός Ναός Αγίου Παντελεήμονος), is a Greek Orthodox church located in Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of Greece. items.title: Santa Maria della Pietà
items.fact: The church of Santa Maria della Pietà or della Visitazione is a prominent church in the sestiere of Castello in Venice, Italy. It is sited on the Riva degli Schiavoni, a short walk from the Doge's Palace.

items.title: Santa Maria Maddalena
items.fact: The Santa Maria Maddalena is a Catholic church in Rome, Italy dedicated to Saint Mary Magdalene. It is the conventual church of the adjacent General Curia of the Clerks Regular, Ministers to the Sick (Camillians), the world headquarters of the order.

items.title: Abbey of St Genevieve
items.fact: The Abbey of Saint Genevieve (French: Abbaye Sainte-Geneviève) was a monastery in Paris. Reportedly built by Clovis, King of the Franks in 502, it became a centre of religious scholarship in the Middle Ages.

items.title: Chapel of the Snows
items.fact: The Chapel of the Snows is a non-denominational Christian church at the United States' McMurdo Station on Ross Island, Antarctica. Initially built from scrap material in 1956, it burned down in 1978 and was rebuilt in 1989.

items.fact: The Church of Our Lady of Victories at the Sablon (French: Église Notre-Dame des Victoires au Sablon; Dutch: Onze-Lieve-Vrouw ter Zege op de Zavelkerk), or the Church of Our Lady of the Sablon (French: Église Notre-Dame du Sablon; Dutch: Onze-Lieve-Vrouw ter Zavelkerk), is a Catholic church in the Sablon/Zavel district of Brussels, Belgium.

items.fact: Bogdana Monastery is a Romanian Orthodox monastery in the town of Rădăuți, northern Romania. Its church is the oldest still standing religious building in Moldavia.

items.fact: The Marktkirche Unser Lieben Frauen ("Market Church of Our Dear Lady") is a church in the centre of the city of Halle, Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. It was built between 1529 and 1554 and is the most recent of the city's medieval churches.

items.title: Notre-Dame-de-Lorette (Paris)

items.fact: San Michele in Foro is a Roman Catholic basilica church in Lucca, Tuscany, central Italy, built over the ancient Roman forum. Until 1370 it was the seat of the Consiglio Maggiore ("Major Council"), the commune's most important assembly.

items.fact: Triq il-Wiesgħa Tower (Maltese: Torri ta' Triq il-Wiesgħa), originally known as Torre della Giddida and also called Mwejġel Tower (Maltese: Torri ta' Mwejġel or Torri tal-Imwiegħel), is a small watchtower near Żabbar, Malta. items.fact: The Church of the Holy Apostles (Greek: Ἅγιοι Ἀπόστολοι) is a 14th-century Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church in the city of Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of northern Greece.

items.title: Timotesubani
items.fact: Timotesubani (Georgian: ტიმოთესუბანი) is a medieval Georgian Orthodox Christian monastic complex located at the eponymous village in the Borjomi Gorge, Georgia's Samtskhe-Javakheti region.

items.title: San Bernardino alle Ossa
items.fact: San Bernardino alle Ossa is a church in Milan, northern Italy, best known for its ossuary, a small side chapel decorated with numerous human skulls and bones. In 1210, when an adjacent cemetery ran out of space, a room was built to hold bones.

items.title: Chiesa di San Pantalon
items.fact: The Chiesa di San Pantaleone Martire, known as San Pantalon in the Venetian language, is a church in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy. It is located on the Campo San Pantalon (square), and is dedicated to Saint Pantaleon.

items.title: Minoritenkirche
items.fact: The Minoritenkirche (English: Friars Minor Conventual Church, related to the monastic Order of Friars Minor Conventual monks), formally called Italienische Nationalkirche Maria Schnee (English: Italian National Church of Mary of the Snows, related to the Italian Congregation who was the owner of this church), was built in French Gothic style in the Altstadt or First District of Vienna, Austria.

items.title: Jesuit Church
items.fact: The Mannheim Jesuit Church is a Catholic church of historic and artistic importance in Mannheim, Germany. Church construction was begun in 1733 and completed in 1760.

items.title: Church of Saint Catherine, Thessaloniki
items.fact: The Church of Saint Catherine (Greek: Αγία Αικατερίνη) is a late Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church in the northwestern corner of the Ano Poli, Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of Greece.

items.title: Church of Prophet Elijah
items.fact: The Church of Prophet Elijah (Greek: Ναός Προφήτη Ηλία, romanized: Naós Profíti Ilía) is a 14th-century Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church in the Ano Poli neighbourhood of the city of Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of northern Greece.

items.title: Le Zitelle
items.fact: Le Zitelle (officially Santa Maria della Presentazione), or “The Spinsters” is a church in Venice, Italy. It is part of a former complex which gave shelter to young maidens ("zitelle" in Italian) who had no dowry, and is on the eastern part of the Giudecca island.

items.title: Odzun Church
items.fact: Odzun Church (Armenian: Օձունի եկեղեցի) is an Armenian basilica constructed around the 5th–7th century in the Odzun village of the Lori Province of Armenia.

items.title: Santi Luca e Martina
items.fact: Santi Luca e Martina is a church in Rome, Italy, situated between the Roman Forum and the Forum of Caesar and close to the Arch of Septimus Severus.

items.title: St. Cyriakus
items.fact: Saint Cyriakus (German: Stiftskirche St. Cyriakus, pronounced [ˈʃtɪftsˌkɪʁçə zaŋkt tsyˈʁi̯aːkʊs]) is a medieval church in Gernrode, Saxony-Anhalt, Germany.

items.title: Abbey of Santa Giustina
items.fact: The Abbey of Santa Giustina is a 10th-century Benedictine abbey complex located in front of the Prato della Valle in central Padua, region of Veneto, Italy. Adjacent to the former monastery is the basilica church of Santa Giustina, initially built in the 6th century, but whose present form derives from a 17th-century reconstruction.

items.title: Temple of Minerva
items.fact: The Temple of Minerva (Italian: Tempio di Minerva) is an ancient Roman building located in Assisi, Umbria, central Italy. Since 1539, it has housed the church of Santa Maria sopra Minerva, which was renovated in the Baroque style during the 17th century.

items.title: Bürgersaalkirche
items.fact: The Bürgersaal (English: "Citizen's Hall") is a historical building in Munich, Germany. Also known as Bürgersaalkirche since the consecration of the altar on May 13, 1778, it is the prayer and meeting room of the Marian Men Congregation "Annunciation".

items.title: San Nicolò dei Mendicoli
items.fact: San Nicolò dei Mendicoli ("Saint Nicholas of the Beggars") is a church, which is located in the sestiere of Dorsoduro in Venice.

items.title: Basilica of the Holy Trinity, Kraków
items.fact: The Church of the Holy Trinity (Polish: Kościół Świętej Trójcy), known colloquially as the Dominicans Church (Polish: Kościół dominikanów) is a historic Roman Catholic conventual church of the Order of Preachers located at 12 Stolarska Street in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

items.title: Catholic Church of Our Lady of the Rosary
items.fact: The Catholic Church of Our Lady of the Rosary (Arabic: كنيسة سيدة المسبحة) is a Catholic church in Doha, Qatar. It is located, along with churches of other Christian denominations, at the Religious Complex in Abu Hamour.

items.title: Church of Peace
items.fact: The Protestant Church of Peace (German: Friedenskirche) is situated in the Marly Gardens on the Green Fence (Am Grünen Gitter) in the palace grounds of Sanssouci Park in Potsdam, Germany.

items.title: Hedal Stave Church
items.fact: Hedalen Stave Church (Norwegian: Hedalen stavkyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Sør-Aurdal Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The stave church is located in the Hedalen valley.

items.title: Piarist Church
items.fact: The Piarist Church, also known as the Church of Maria Treu, is a Baroque parish church of the Order of the Piarists (Patres Scholarum Piarum) in Vienna, Austria. It is located in Vienna's 8th district (Josefstadt).

items.title: Church of the Holy Trinity
items.fact: The Articular church in Kežmarok (Slovak: Artikulárny kostol v Kežmarku) is a wooden church in Kežmarok, Slovakia.

items.title: Saint Nicholas Concathedral
items.fact: The Co-Cathedral of Saint Nicholas (Slovak: Konkatedrála svätého Mikuláša) in Prešov is one of the oldest and most important churches in Slovakia. The external dimensions of the cathedral are 54.7m in length and 34.45m in width.

items.title: San Nazaro in Brolo
items.fact: The basilica of San Nazaro in Brolo or San Nazaro Maggiore is a 4th-century Roman Catholic church located in Piazza San Nazzaro in Brolo in Milan, region of Lombardy, Italy.

items.title: Temple of St. Michael Archangel
items.fact: Church of Saint Michael the Archangel of Ladomirová is a Greek-catholic church situated in the village of Ladomirová.

items.title: Torre dei Lamberti
items.fact: The Torre dei Lamberti is an 84 m high tower in Verona, northern Italy. Construction of the tower began in 1172.

items.title: Menshikov Tower
items.fact: Menshikov Tower (Russian: Меншикова башня), also known as the Church of Archangel Gabriel, is a Baroque Russian Orthodox Church in Basmanny District of Moscow, within the Boulevard Ring.

items.title: Methodist Central Hall
items.fact: The Methodist Central Hall (also known as Central Hall Westminster) is a multi-purpose venue in the City of Westminster, serving primarily as a Methodist church and a conference centre.

items.title: San Giorgio Maggiore, Naples
items.fact: San Giorgio Maggiore is a basilica church located on the corner of Via vicaria Vecchia and Via Duomo, in central Naples, Italy. The apse of the church lies diagonally across the street from San Severo al Pendino.

items.title: Noorderkerk
items.fact: The Noorderkerk (Dutch for "northern church") is a 17th-century Protestant church in Amsterdam, The Netherlands. The Noorderkerk is located along Prinsengracht canal, on Noordermarkt square.

items.title: church Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis of Paris
items.fact: The Église Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis (French pronunciation: [eɡliz sɛ̃ pɔl sɛ̃ lwi]) is a church on rue Saint-Antoine in the Marais quarter of Paris. The present building was constructed from 1627 to 1641 by the Jesuit architects Étienne and François Derand, on the orders of Louis XIII.

items.title: Saint-Nicholas-des-Champs, Paris
items.fact: The Church of Saint-Nicolas-des-Champs (French: Église Saint-Nicolas-des-Champs; literally, St Nicholas-in-the-Fields) is a Catholic church in Paris' Third arrondissement.

items.title: Church of St. James the Greater
items.fact: The Basilica of St. James (Czech: Bazilika svatého Jakuba Většího) in the Old Town of Prague, Czech Republic.

items.title: San Gioacchino ai Prati di Castello
items.fact: San Gioacchino ai Prati di Castello ("St Joachim's at the Fields of the Castle") is a church in Rome dedicated to Saint Joachim, the father of Mary, mother of Jesus. Construction began in 1891 and the building was opened to the public in 1898.

items.title: St. Peter
items.fact: Old St. Peter's Church (German: Alte Peterskirche) is a Lutheran parish and church in the old town of Leipzig, Germany.

items.title: Christuskirche
items.fact: The Christuskirche is a Lutheran Evangelical church in Rome. It was built between 1910 and 1922 under the direction of architect Franz Heinrich Schwechten, who was also responsible for the Kaiser-Wilhelm-Gedächtniskirche in Berlin.

items.title: Sant'Antonio dei Portoghesi
items.fact: The church of Saint Anthony in Campo Marzio, known as Saint Anthony of the Portuguese (Italian: Sant'Antonio dei Portoghesi, Portuguese: Santo António dos Portugueses), is a Baroque Roman Catholic titular church in Rome, dedicated to Saint Anthony of Lisbon.

items.title: Santa Maria del Carmine
items.fact: Santa Maria del Carmine (Our Lady of Mount Carmel) is a church in Naples, Italy. It is at one end of Piazza Mercato (Market Square), the centre of civic life in Naples for many centuries until it was cut off from the rest of the city by urban renewal in 1900.
